seo_title: Visual launchd job editor for macOS
seo_description: LaunchdLens is a free, open-source macOS app to browse, create and schedule launchd agents with a form editor and live status. No plist hand-editing.
hero_sub: Browse your launch agents, edit them in a validated form, and schedule scripts in plain terms. Press ⌘N to start a new job from a template.
features_sub: A focused editor for per-user launch agents, built only on Apple frameworks.

features.title: Live status for every agent
features.desc: The sidebar lists ~/Library/LaunchAgents with a colored dot: running with PID, loaded, failed with last exit code, or not loaded. It refreshes every 3 seconds.

features.title: Form editor with validation
features.desc: Edit label, program, arguments, run at load, keep alive, intervals, watch paths and log paths. Red notes flag bad labels, missing programs and invalid values as you type.

features.title: Schedules in plain language
features.desc: Presets like every weekday expand into StartCalendarInterval entries, and the app reads them back, for example "Runs every weekday at 09:00."

features.title: Templates and one-click actions
features.desc: Start from a template for scheduled scripts, login items, keep-alive apps or folder watchers. Then Save, Load, Unload, Run Now or Delete using launchctl.

features.title: Raw plist, print and logs
features.desc: Inspect the generated property list and the launchctl print output. The log viewer tails your job's output file and refreshes every 2 seconds.

features.title: Careful with existing files
features.desc: Unknown keys survive a round trip, writes are atomic, and you are warned before overwriting files the app did not create. Deleted jobs are unloaded first and moved to the Trash.

faq.q: Is LaunchdLens really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is in the GitHub repository. There are no accounts, no ads and no paid tier; an optional Support button links to Ko-fi.

None of the privacy-controlled kind: no Accessibility, Screen Recording, Camera, Microphone, Contacts or Location. It reads and writes your LaunchAgents folder and runs /bin/launchctl as your own user. If a job's script touches protected folders, macOS may ask when that job runs.

Your jobs are ordinary .plist files in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, so other tools can read them too. The app's own preferences, such as the label prefix, live in UserDefaults. Nothing is sent over the network.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
